description: Reinforced Concrete Coupling Beams with High-Strength Steel Bars is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Andres Lepage, University of Kansas (ku.edu). The use of high-strength steel bars in reinforced concrete coupling beams has the potential to reduce reinforcement congestion and support more efficient design and construction methods. A series of tests was conducted to investigate the effects of high-strength reinforcement on coupling beam behavior. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: high strength steel, high-strength steel, reinforced concrete, coupling beams, cyclic loading, seismic. Published 2020-09-28. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
